action_name: Improve heat and energy recovery
description: Enhanced energy efficiency in industrial processes by recovering heat and energy from waste streams, improving process coupling, and adopting advanced technologies such as coke dry quenching, black liquor gasification, and top pressure recovery turbines. Includes reducing energy use in comminution, paper drying, and other industrial processes through optimized designs, operational improvements, and material efficiency strategies.
dependencies: Availability of funding or subsidies to support solar energy installations in industries.\nTechnical expertise and capacity for the installation of solar panels and related systems.\nRegulatory frameworks that facilitate the integration of solar energy into industrial operations.
key_performance_indicators: Total greenhouse gas emissions avoided through solar energy adoption in industries (tons of CO₂/year).\nAverage return on investment (ROI) period for industrial solar installations (years).\nPercentage of industrial energy needs met by solar power systems (%).

action_name: Promote and expand the use of the Brazilian Energy Labeling Program for Buildings
description: The city will encourage the adoption and enforcement of the Brazilian Energy Labeling Program for Buildings to improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions from the building sector. The program evaluates and certifies buildings based on their energy performance, covering aspects such as thermal efficiency, lighting, and HVAC systems. Actions may include incentivizing developers and property owners to seek certification, integrating energy performance criteria into municipal building codes, and raising public awareness of the benefits of energy-efficient construction and renovation.
dependencies: Establish clear standards and regulations for energy efficiency labeling.\nLaunch public awareness campaigns and provide incentives for buildings to obtain labels.\nOffer training for building managers to improve energy performance and adoption of labels.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of new buildings with an A rating on the energy efficiency label.\nEstimated reduction in emissions (tCO₂e/year) due to the energy efficiency of labeled buildings.

action_name: Develop integrated renewable energy planning and solar–battery microgrids for rural and peri-urban areas
description: The city will promote integrated regional energy planning to ensure that electricity expansion in rural and peri-urban areas is cost-effective, low-emission, and equitable. This approach combines renewable energy generation (e.g., solar PV and wind) with battery storage and microgrid systems to extend reliable access to electricity where traditional grid expansion is unviable or inefficient. Municipalities can partner with energy utilities, rural cooperatives, and neighboring jurisdictions to identify optimal locations for solar–battery microgrids or distributed renewable infrastructure, especially in areas adjoining urban centers where land availability supports clean energy generation for both city and rural users. Financing mechanisms may include public–private artnerships (PPPs), leasing models, concessional loans, and power purchase agreements (PPAs).
dependencies: Availability of funding and financial mechanisms to support the installation of renewable energy systems in rural areas\nDevelopment of infrastructure, such as microgrids, to ensure reliable electricity distribution in remote communities\nCollaboration with local governments, energy providers, and community organizations to facilitate the implementation and maintenance of renewable energy solutions in underserved regions
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of rural areas electrified with renewable energy.\nInstalled capacity of renewable energy systems in rural areas (MW).\nAnnual reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from rural electrification projects.

action_name: Enable smart grid integration and distributed energy storage through municipal collaboration and demonstration projects
description: The city will collaborate with energy utilities, regulators, and technology providers to support the deployment of smart grid infrastructure and distributed energy storage systems that enhance flexibility, reliability, and renewable energy integration. While large-scale grid modernization is typically led by national or regional authorities
dependencies: Investment in the development and deployment of smart grids and energy storage technologies to improve energy management\nTechnical expertise and infrastructure to integrate renewable energy sources into the smart grid and ensure effective energy storage\nPolicy and regulatory frameworks to support the widespread adoption of smart grids and energy storage systems, including incentives and grid integration standards
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of the grid covered by smart grid technology.\nInstalled capacity of energy storage systems (MW or MWh).\nReduction in energy losses across the grid (%).

action_name: Deploy cogeneration systems in industries
description: Utilize combined heat and power systems to maximize energy efficiency in industrial processes.
dependencies: Availability of technical expertise and resources to design and implement combined heat and power (CHP) systems in industrial processes\nInvestment in infrastructure to integrate CHP systems into existing industrial facilities and processes\nPolicy and regulatory support to incentivize the adoption of energy-efficient technologies like CHP systems in the industrial sector
key_performance_indicators: Installed capacity of cogeneration systems in industrial facilities (MW).\nAnnual energy generated and used from cogeneration systems (kWh/year).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from industrial cogeneration.

action_name: Promote Net-Zero and Green Building Certifications
description: This action focuses on promoting sustainable buildings by supporting net-zero energy goals and encouraging green building certifications such as LEED. It aims to incentivize the construction and renovation of buildings that produce as much energy as they consume, reducing their environmental impact. This initiative also fosters the adoption of sustainable practices and technologies, ensuring long-term energy efficiency and environmental responsibility across residential, commercial, and public infrastructure.
dependencies: Availability of financial incentives, subsidies, or tax credits to encourage homeowners to install solar, wind, and other clean energy systems\nAccess to information and educational resources to help homeowners understand the benefits, costs, and installation processes for clean energy systems\nDevelopment of supportive regulations and policies that facilitate the installation of renewable energy technologies in residential areas
key_performance_indicators: Number of buildings certified as net-zero or green buildings annually.\nReduction in energy and water consumption in certified buildings (kWh/year, m³/year).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from green building practices.

action_name: Expand solar energy generation on municipal facilities and public assets
description: The city will install and scale up solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on municipal buildings and public assets, including schools, health centers, administrative offices, bus terminals, water treatment plants, and decommissioned landfills. The objective is to increase the share of renewable electricity in municipal operations, lower energy costs, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Facilitating pilot and demonstration projects in municipal buildings, neighborhoods, or industrial zones to showcase the benefits of smart meters, automated controls, and local storage systems; Supporting demand-side flexibility programs, such as time-of-use tariffs and smart appliance initiatives; Incorporating grid-readiness and distributed generation planning into local development and zoning strategies; and \nEngaging in integrated resource planning with utilities to ensure that urban and peri-urban energy needs are aligned with regional grid upgrades.
dependencies: Availability of funding and financial mechanisms to support the installation of solar energy systems in public facilities and remote areas\nDevelopment of infrastructure to support the integration of solar energy systems in underserved regions, including grid connection or off-grid solutions\nCollaboration with local governments, energy providers, and community organizations to ensure effective implementation and maintenance of solar energy systems in these areas
key_performance_indicators: Installed capacity (MW)\nPercentage of remote areas powered by solar energy systems\nAnnual reduction in CO2 equivalent emissions from the adoption of solar energy

action_name: Promote Mini and Micro-Hydropower and Biomass Energy
description: This action focuses on promoting renewable energy generation by developing mini and micro-hydropower plants and encouraging biomass energy production in agricultural regions. By harnessing the potential of local water resources and organic waste, this initiative aims to diversify the energy mix, improve energy security, and support sustainable agricultural practices, reducing dependence on fossil fuels while promoting environmentally friendly energy solutions.
dependencies: Availability of technical expertise and resources to design and implement mini and micro-hydropower plants and biomass energy systems\nAccess to local water resources and organic waste for energy generation, ensuring sustainable sourcing and environmental impact assessment\nPolicy and regulatory frameworks to incentivize the development of renewable energy projects in agricultural regions and ensure their integration into the local energy grid
key_performance_indicators: Installed capacity of mini and micro-hydropower and biomass energy systems (MW).\nAnnual energy generation from these systems (kWh/year).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from replacing fossil fuels with renewable sources.

action_name: Promote solar thermal and heat pump systems for water heating in residential, commercial, and public buildings
description: The city will encourage the adoption of renewable and efficient water heating systems, including solar thermal collectors and heat pumps, across residential, commercial, and public facilities. These systems significantly reduce energy consumption and emissions associated with conventional electric or gas water heating. Municipal actions may include: Installing systems in public buildings (schools, hospitals, sports centers) to demonstrate leadership and reduce operational costs; Providing incentives or financing programs for residential and commercial installations; and Updating building codes or efficiency standards to integrate renewable heating technologies in new and retrofitted constructions.
dependencies: Availability of financial incentives and subsidies to support the installation of solar thermal energy systems in residential, commercial, and public facilities\nDevelopment of technical standards and guidelines to ensure the efficient installation and use of solar thermal systems\nPublic awareness campaigns to educate citizens and businesses on the benefits of solar thermal energy for water heating and its environmental advantages
key_performance_indicators: Number of new solar thermal systems installed annually.\nReduction in energy consumption from conventional water heating systems (kWh/year).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from the adoption of solar thermal energy.

action_name: Upgrade and maintain electrical substations
description: Enhance the reliability and efficiency of the electrical grid by modernizing substation equipment and implementing regular maintenance programs.
dependencies: Availability of funding and resources to modernize substation equipment and upgrade grid infrastructure\nAccess to technical expertise for the implementation of advanced grid technologies and regular maintenance protocols\nPolicy and regulatory support to ensure consistent maintenance schedules and integrate modern equipment into the existing electrical grid
key_performance_indicators: Reduction in energy transmission losses (%).\nIncreased reliability and uptime of the electrical grid (%).

action_name: Integrate renewables into municipal water systems
description: Implement renewable energy sources, such as solar or wind power, to drive water treatment, pumping, and distribution systems, reducing energy costs and emissions.
dependencies: Availability of funding or financial incentives to integrate renewable energy sources like solar or wind power into water treatment and distribution systems\nTechnical expertise and infrastructure to retrofit existing systems with renewable energy solutions or design new facilities powered by renewables\nPolicy and regulatory support to encourage the use of clean energy in water systems and ensure its integration into municipal energy grids
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of municipal water systems powered by renewables.\nReduction in energy consumption from non-renewable sources (kWh/year).\nGHG emissions avoided (tons CO₂e)

action_name: Promote energy-efficient and climate-resilient housing for low-income and informal settlements
description: The city will develop and support housing programs that integrate energy-efficient and climate-resilient design principles, reducing energy costs and improving comfort for low-income households and residents of informal settlements. Measures may include the use of thermal insulation materials, reflective roofing, natural ventilation, and efficient lighting and appliances (such as LEDs and solar water heaters). Municipal actions can involve incentivizing retrofits, integrating efficiency criteria into social housing programs, and offering technical assistance or subsidies for small-scale upgrades. This action can be combined with broader improvement projects that address sanitation, water access, and structural safety, fostering integrated and inclusive neighborhood upgrading. These interventions enhance quality of life, reduce energy poverty, and contribute to urban climate mitigation and adaptation goals.
dependencies: Availability of funding or subsidies to support the development of energy-efficient housing for low-income households\nCollaboration with architects, engineers, and contractors to design and implement energy-efficient technologies in housing projects\nDevelopment of policies and regulations to incentivize energy-efficient housing solutions and ensure affordability for low-income communities
key_performance_indicators: Number of energy-efficient housing units built or retrofitted.\nReduction in household energy consumption (kWh).\nDecrease in energy bills for low-income households (USD).

action_name: Implement time-of-use electricity tariffs to enhance demand-side flexibility and efficiency
description: The city will work with energy regulators and utilities to introduce time-of-use (TOU) electricity tariffs that incentivize consumers to shift energy use toward off-peak hours. By encouraging demand-side flexibility, this measure helps to balance grid demand, ensure grid stability, and lower energy costs for consumers, particularly when combined with energy-efficient appliances and smart metering technologies. Municipal roles may include advocating for regulatory approval, piloting TOU programs in public facilities, and raising awareness among residential, commercial, and industrial users. This action supports the city’s broader energy efficiency and resilience objectives, helping to integrate renewable energy more effectively and reduce peak load pressures.
dependencies: Development of pricing models, such as time-of-use rates, to encourage energy consumption during off-peak hours\nCollaboration with utility companies to implement and communicate the new pricing structures effectively to consumers\nRegulatory support to ensure the pricing structures align with grid management goals and incentivize energy use without disadvantaging vulnerable populations
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of households enrolled in time-of-use tariff programs.\nReduction in peak electricity demand (%).\nAnnual reduction in GHG emissions due to optimized energy use (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Create financing programs for local renewable energy projects
description: Establish funding mechanisms, such as grants and low-interest loans, to support the development of small-scale renewable energy initiatives in communities. These programs can also support community renewable energy farms and cooperatives, enabling shared access to clean power and strengthening local ownership models.
dependencies: "Development of accessible financial mechanisms, including grants and low-interest loans, to support small-scale renewable energy projects in communities","Collaboration with financial institutions and local governments to ensure the effective disbursement and management of funding for renewable energy initiatives","Clear guidelines and support for community organizations and local businesses to access funding and successfully implement renewable energy projects","Acceso a conocimientos técnicos y recursos para orientar la instalación y el mantenimiento de sistemas de energía eólica en entornos residenciales y comunitarios."
key_performance_indicators: "Development of accessible financial mechanisms, including grants and low-interest loans, to support small-scale renewable energy projects in communities","Collaboration with financial institutions and local governments to ensure the effective disbursement and management of funding for renewable energy initiatives","Clear guidelines and support for community organizations and local businesses to access funding and successfully implement renewable energy projects","Acceso a conocimientos técnicos y recursos para orientar la instalación y el mantenimiento de sistemas de energía eólica en entornos residenciales y comunitarios."

action_name: Promote passive cooling through natural shading and ventilation in residential, commercial, and public buildings
description: The city will require or encourage passive cooling design features—including shaded facades, green roofs, natural ventilation, reflective surfaces, and cross-ventilation layouts—to reduce dependence on mechanical air conditioning in residential, commercial, and public buildings. These measures improve indoor comfort, lower energy demand, and enhance urban resilience to heat stress. Implementation can include updating building codes, incentivizing retrofits, and providing design guidance for new developments and renovations. This action complements other green building initiatives and supports long-term climate adaptation through energy efficiency and thermal comfort.
dependencies: Development of building design guidelines and standards that promote the integration of passive cooling features like shaded facades, green roofs, and cross-ventilation\nAvailability of financial incentives or support for incorporating energy-efficient architectural features in both new and existing buildings\nCollaboration with architects, urban planners, and local authorities to integrate these features into urban development and renovation projects
key_performance_indicators: Number of buildings incorporating natural shading/ventilation.\nReduction in cooling energy demand (%) per building.\nTemperature resilience improvements in monitored buildings (°C).

action_name: Capture & Use Biogas at Wastewater Treatment Plants'
description: Install biogas systems in wastewater treatment facilities to produce renewable energy from organic sludge, reducing emissions and operational costs. Technologies may include sludge digestion, CHP for plant loads, and upgrading to biomethane for vehicles. This action can be financed by development banks and can be scaled by regionalization.
dependencies: Availability of funding or subsidies to support the installation of biogas systems in wastewater treatment facilities\nAccess to technical expertise to design and integrate biogas systems into existing treatment processes\nRegulatory frameworks that incentivize renewable energy generation from wastewater treatment and ensure compliance with environmental standards
key_performance_indicators: Volume of biogas produced annually (m³).\nPercentage of wastewater treatment plants using biogas systems.\nGHG emissions avoided by biogas use (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Install biodigesters in rural properties
description: Equip rural farms and properties with biodigesters to convert organic waste into biogas and nutrient-rich fertilizers, providing a sustainable energy source.
dependencies: Availability of funding or subsidies to support the installation of biodigesters on rural farms and properties\nAccess to technical expertise for the design, installation, and maintenance of biodigesters\nDevelopment of a supportive regulatory framework that encourages the use of biogas and organic waste management systems in rural agriculture
key_performance_indicators: Volume of biogas generated (m³/year).\nGHG emissions avoided by replacing fossil fuels (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Improve Fuel Supply Systems for Industrial Heating
description: Enhancing fuel delivery systems in the steel production process by implementing technologies such as pulverized coal injection, improving furnace designs and process controls, and optimizing fuel combustion for heating. Includes energy efficiency measures to reduce emissions from coal and coke used in conventional iron-making, and the potential adoption of alternative reductants like biomass and waste plastics.
dependencies: Development of a tax incentive framework targeting clean technology investments.\nAvailability of financial resources for subsidies and tax incentives.\nCollaboration between government and businesses to identify eligible clean technologies.
key_performance_indicators: Average percentage of tax savings per company adopting clean technologies (%).\nNumber of new clean technology companies established as a result of tax incentives.\nIncrease in clean technology-related jobs created due to tax incentives.

action_name: Enhance industrial energy efficiency processes
description: Implement advanced technologies and process optimizations in industrial facilities to minimize energy consumption and improve productivity.
dependencies: Availability of financial incentives or support to invest in advanced technologies and process optimizations in industrial facilities\nAccess to technical expertise and resources to implement energy-efficient solutions and optimize industrial processes\nCollaboration with industry stakeholders and regulatory frameworks to encourage the adoption of energy-saving technologies and ensure compliance with sustainability goals
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of industries adopting energy-efficient technologies.\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from energy-efficient industrial processes.

action_name: Deploy energy-efficient and solar-powered street lighting across all neighborhoods
description: The city will install LED-based (or other low emission technologies), solar-powered streetlights in all neighborhoods, including rural and peri-urban areas, to enhance safety, accessibility, and social inclusion while reducing energy costs and environmental impacts. Where feasible, the action prioritizes solar power generation, especially in areas with limited grid coverage or high carbon intensity. In locations where the electricity grid is already clean, the focus will be on maximizing lighting efficiency through LED retrofits and smart controls. Municipal roles include procuring equipment, establishing public–private financing mechanisms, and contracting long-term maintenance services to ensure system reliability. This action delivers strong co-benefits for communities of all sizes but requires careful planning to address maintenance and operational challenges.
dependencies: Availability of funding or financial mechanisms to support the installation of solar-powered streetlights in rural communities\nAccess to technical expertise to design, install, and maintain solar-powered street lighting systems\nCollaboration with local governments and communities to ensure the integration of solar streetlights into existing infrastructure and energy plans
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of streetlights powered by solar energy.\nAnnual reduction in electricity consumption (kWh).\nGHG emissions avoided (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Promote organic, regenerative and agroecological agriculture in rural areas
description: Promote organic, regenerative and agroecological agricultural principles in the rural areas of the city. This can include reducing reliance on chemical pesticides, improving soil health and promoting carbon sequestration in the soil. Actions could include providing technical training and educational programmes for rural producers, using economic instruments to incentivize agroecological conversion, and creating resources or networks for skill sharing. Work cooperatively with rural producers, including engaging with Indigenous practises and skillsets.
dependencies: Availability of technical training programs for farmers to adopt organic and agroecological practices\nStrengthened value chains and market access for agroecological products to ensure economic sustainability\nImplementation of economic instruments, such as payment for environmental services, to incentivize agroecological conversion
key_performance_indicators: Number of sustainable rural economic projects implemented annually.\nReduction in environmental impact from traditional farming or production practices (%).\nPercentage of rural households adopting sustainable practices.

action_name: Develop regional hubs for renewable energy production
description: Establish strategic centers for large-scale renewable energy generation, supporting local economies and providing reliable, clean energy to surrounding areas.
dependencies: Establishment of strategic centers for large-scale renewable energy generation.\nSupport for local economies through renewable energy initiatives.\nProvision of reliable and clean energy to surrounding areas.
key_performance_indicators: Installed renewable energy capacity in hubs (MW).\nNumber of jobs created in the renewable energy sector.\nAnnual GHG emissions avoided by renewable energy generation (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Accelerate the adoption of Agroforestry'
description: Promote agroforestry systems by integrating trees into food cultivation and pasture, increasing biodiversity and carbon sequestration. Agroforestry integrates trees and shrubs with crops and/or livestock to sequester carbon, enhance soil health, reduce soil erosion, improve water quality, and diversify livelihoods. It also offers co-benefits like mitigating regional climates and increasing land productivity while addressing risks like biodiversity and hydrology impacts. Agroforestry systems can include silvopastoral systems, alley cropping, riparian buffer planting. Create financial and technical incentives for integrating agroforestry practices into livestock systems.
dependencies: Provision of technical support and guidance to farmers on the design and implementation of agroforestry systems.\nDevelopment of financial incentives or subsidies to make agroforestry more economically attractive.\nCreation of policies that integrate agroforestry practices into agricultural land-use planning and land tenure systems.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of agricultural land converted to agroforestry systems (%).\nNumber of new agroforestry projects implemented.\nIncrease in carbon sequestration in agroforestry systems (tons of CO₂e/year).

action_name: Support cooperatives of voluntary waste collectors to aggregate into small enterprises and expand into organics management
description: Measures to aggregate voluntary waste collectors into small enterprises or associtations, improve working conditions and income in the processes of sorting recyclable and organic waste to contribute for GHG emissions reduction and the increase climate risk resilience. It includes mapping individual and groups of voluntary waste collectors, provide training for collectors in waste management and treatement technologies, economics, business management, and conceptual planning for the operation and administration of the Sorting Unit.
dependencies: Implementation of measures to improve working conditions and income for recyclable waste sorting.\nOngoing training for collectors in technology, economics, business management, and operational planning.\nDevelopment of administrative and operational capabilities for the Sorting Unit.
key_performance_indicators: Number of cooperatives supported annually.\nIncrease in income of collectors (%).\nVolume of recyclable materials collected by cooperatives (tons/year).

action_name: Develop an organic waste management strategy
description: Development of an organic waste management strategy with near, mid and long term interventions, integrating aquisition and implementation of organic waste treatment technologies and resources to build the adequate infrastructure to treat the collected waste, such as composting, biodigestion and other technologies, in order to reduce the amount sent to landfills and to achieve maximum organics waste diversion
dependencies: "Development of feasibility studies for wet waste treatment technologies.","Exploration of composting and biodigestion to reduce landfill waste.","Assessment of technical and economic viability for implementation.","Provide training and resources to ensure proper waste segregation and processing.","Develop policies and incentives to encourage business and community participation in organic waste management."
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of wet waste treated using new technologies.\nBiogas produced from wet waste treatment (m³/year).\nGHG emissions avoided (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Complete ecological and agroclimatic mapping
description: Use zoning and mapping tools to identify areas best suited for sustainable agriculture and those that require environmental preservation. Incorporate findings into planning or zoning regulations, Economic Plans, Climate Action Plans and associated strategic work or policy design. Include mappings of local Indigenous and smallholder-linked land, public spaces, socio-economic data and other priorities. This will help inform plans to accelerate agroecological production locally and preserve ecologically important areas, and can be a useful tool for engaging stakeholders.
dependencies: Provide access to high-resolution geospatial data and zoning tools for planning.\nIncorporate socio-economic and ecological criteria into the zoning process.\nEngage stakeholders and align zoning with existing regulations and policies.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of territory with implemented agro-climatic and agricultural zoning (%).\nNumber of farms adopting practices recommended in agro-climatic zoning.\nReduction of cultivated areas in high-risk climate zones (hectares or %)"

action_name: Increase efficiency of industrial furnaces and kilns
description: Enhancing the design and operation of furnaces and kilns to improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions. Includes technologies such as improved heat and energy recovery from process gases, advanced process controls, and better furnace designs to minimize temperature cycles and optimize fuel usage.
dependencies: Availability of sustainable materials at competitive prices.\nSupportive policies and regulations promoting material substitution.\nIndustry awareness and capacity to transition to new materials.
key_performance_indicators: Number of public awareness campaigns or training sessions conducted to promote sustainable materials.\nPercentage cost reduction in sustainable material production compared to traditional materials (%).\nMarket share of sustainable materials compared to traditional materials in local industries (%).

action_name: Improve Heat Recovery and Reuse through Heat Exchanger Networks or Heat Pumps
description: This action involves improving heat-use energy efficiency by utilizing heat exchanger networks and high-temperature heat pumps to recover and reuse waste heat in industrial processes. Techniques include reducing heat needs via thermal insulation, reusing waste heat at various temperature grades, and recycling waste heat for power generation through technologies such as mechanical vapor recompression and thermoelectric conversion.
dependencies: Establishment of multi-stakeholder forums involving industry and government.\nDevelopment of clear policy frameworks to support emissions reduction.\nCreation of financial incentives for industries to adopt sustainable practices.
key_performance_indicators: Number of collaborative agreements signed between industry and government.\nAmount of emissions reduced through collaborative initiatives (tons of CO₂/year).\nPercentage of key industries engaged in emissions reduction partnerships (%).

action_name: Adopt industrial energy efficiency technologies
description: Implementation of energy-efficient technologies in mining processes, particularly in comminution, by upgrading ore concentration methods, using efficient grinding and crushing technologies, and optimizing particle size feed. Other opportunities include improving separation, drying, and materials handling processes.
dependencies: Funding for research and development of carbon-neutral technologies.\nPartnerships between government, academia, and industry to foster innovation.\nIncentive programs for industries to adopt new technologies.
key_performance_indicators: Number of research projects funded or initiated.\nPercentage of local industries adopting carbon-neutral technologies (%).\nReduction in carbon emissions in industries participating in research projects (tons of CO₂/year).

action_name: Electrify Industrial Processes (with Renewable Power)
description: Transitioning steel production processes to electrified methods such as molten oxide electrolysis, advanced direct reduction, and other methods powered by low-carbon electricity to reduce emissions and improve energy efficiency.
dependencies: Development of infrastructure for biofuel and hydrogen production and distribution.\nRegulatory frameworks to support the transition to low-carbon fuels.\nAvailability of technology to integrate biofuels and hydrogen into industrial systems.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of industrial energy consumption from low-emission fuels (%).\nReduction in GHG emissions from fuel substitution (tons of CO₂e/year).\nNumber of facilities transitioning to low-emission fuel sources

action_name: Decarbonize industrial feedstocks
description: Decarbonising feedstocks for industrial processes through Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS), Carbon Capture and Utilisation (CCU), and integration with low-carbon energy sources. This includes capturing carbon from various industrial emissions and reusing or storing it to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Applications include creating synthetic fuels, chemicals, and materials while using renewable energy or biogenic carbon sources.
dependencies: Clear waste management regulations for industries.\nAvailability of waste processing infrastructure.\nTraining programs for industrial workers on waste management.
key_performance_indicators: Reduction in hazardous waste generation (tons/year).\nIncrease in the recycling rate of industrial waste materials (%).\nAmount of waste-to-energy conversion achieved (MWh/year)

action_name: Implement carbon capture and utilization (CCU)
description: Capturing CO₂ from industrial processes or combustion gases and reusing it for producing fuels, chemicals, and building materials, reducing emissions from the initial source and substituting new fossil/biogenic feedstocks. Prioritize CCU for residual emissions and for end-uses with robust MRV and, where possible, durable carbon retention; do not displace higher-priority efficiency and material circularity measures.
dependencies: Availability of qualified professionals or energy auditors to conduct thorough assessments across industries and buildings.\nDevelopment of a standardized framework for energy audits, ensuring consistency and accuracy in results.\nImplementation of government or corporate incentives to encourage organizations to act on audit recommendations, such as rebates for energy-efficient upgrades.
key_performance_indicators: Number of industrial plants conducting energy audits annually.\nCost savings achieved through audit-recommended improvements (%).\nAverage time to implement energy efficiency measures post-audit (months).

action_name: Implement carbon capture and storage (CCS)
description: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) involves capturing CO₂ from industrial processes, energy generation, or the atmosphere and storing it in geological formations for millennia. CCS can enable near-zero or negative emissions when combined with sustainably sourced biofuels or direct air capture. Apply CCS primarily to residual/process emissions (e.g., calcination) after efficiency, circularity, and electrification have been pursued where feasible.
dependencies: Provision of incentives, such as tax breaks or subsidies, to make renewable energy technologies more affordable for industries.\nDevelopment of infrastructure for the integration of renewable energy into existing industrial operations, including energy storage solutions.\nTechnical assistance and training for industry stakeholders to facilitate the transition to renewable energy sources.
key_performance_indicators: Number of industries adopting renewable energy sources.\nInstalled capacity of renewable energy in industrial operations (MW).\nReduction in average energy costs for industries that transitioned to renewables (%).

action_name: Increase local participation in Agroecological Certification Programmes
description: Agroecological product certifications confirm products meet sustainability criteria and have low environmental impact. Certifications may help rural producers to understand sustainable practices, improve their use of sustainable practices, and increase demand for their products. Actions include creating a dedicated local programme, starting a partnership with an existing certification programme, or raising awareness of certification options and routes to compliance among local producers.
dependencies: Development of clear and accessible certification standards for agroecological products that emphasize sustainability and low environmental impact.\nSupport for farmers and producers to meet certification requirements through training, financial assistance, or technical guidance.\nCreation of marketing strategies and partnerships to increase the visibility and demand for certified agroecological products in local and global markets.
key_performance_indicators: Number of farmers or producers obtaining agroecological certifications.\nPercentage of certified agricultural products in the market (%).\nReduction in the use of synthetic inputs (e.g., fertilizers, pesticides).

action_name: Accelerate the adoption of Zero Emission Agricultural Machinery
description:
Support the transition to zero-emission agricultural machinery, such as tractors and equipment powered by renewable electricity or solar energy. These technologies eliminate greenhouse gas emissions, reduce harmful air pollution and noise, and offer opportunities to modernize and improve agricultural tools and practices. Cities and regions can take multiple actions to accelerate this transition, including:
- Replacing existing municipal machinery with zero-emission alternatives.
- Establishing equipment leasing or sharing schemes to increase accessibility.
- Launching local awareness campaigns through training, education, and communication channels.
- Creating financial incentive or loan programs to encourage adoption.
- Partnering with manufacturers and organizing fairs or demonstrations to showcase zero-emission technologies and other sustainable agricultural solutions to local producers.
dependencies: Establishment of funding programs or incentives for farmers to purchase low-carbon agricultural machinery.\nDevelopment of partnerships with machinery manufacturers to create and distribute sustainable equipment solutions.\nImplementation of training and support programs to assist farmers in integrating and maintaining low-carbon agricultural machinery.
key_performance_indicators: Reduction in emissions from agricultural machinery (tons of CO₂e/year).\nNumber of low-emission machinery subsidies or incentives provided.\nPercentage of farmers trained to operate low-emission machinery.

action_name: Adopt hybrid renewable energy systems (solar-wind)
description: Combine solar and wind energy technologies to create reliable, diversified renewable energy systems suitable for various environmental conditions.
dependencies: Availability of financial resources to invest in combined solar and wind energy systems and infrastructure\nAccess to technical expertise for designing and implementing hybrid renewable energy systems tailored to specific environmental conditions\nDevelopment of supportive policies and regulatory frameworks to integrate solar and wind technologies into the energy grid and ensure their efficient operation
key_performance_indicators: Total hybrid system capacity installed (MW).\nPercentage of energy demand met by hybrid systems.\nAnnual reduction in GHG emissions (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Reduce technical losses in energy distribution networks
description: Upgrade and maintain electrical infrastructure to minimize energy lost during transmission and distribution, improving overall grid efficiency.
dependencies: Availability of funding to invest in modernizing electrical infrastructure and upgrading transmission and distribution networks\nAccess to technical expertise for implementing upgrades that reduce energy losses and improve grid efficiency\nPolicy and regulatory frameworks to ensure ongoing maintenance and integration of energy-efficient technologies into the grid infrastructure
key_performance_indicators: Percentage reduction in technical losses from baseline (%).\nEnergy savings achieved annually (kWh).\nGHG emissions avoided through reduced energy losses (tons CO₂e).

action_name: Regulate Construction and Demolition Waste Management to improve deconstruction, segregation at source, reutilization and recycling
description: Establish comprehensive guidelines for the sustainable management of construction and demolition waste (CDW) to promote efficiency, circularity, and environmental responsibility across the construction sector. The action aims to reduce waste generation at the source, encourage selective deconstruction instead of conventional demolition, and foster material segregation, reuse, and recycling.\n\nThese guidelines should define technical standards, responsibilities, and incentives for all stakeholders involved — including contractors, developers, and waste operators — to ensure that valuable materials such as concrete, metals, wood, and aggregates are recovered and reintegrated into new construction cycles. The framework should also establish procedures for safe handling, transportation, and disposal of non-recyclable materials, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and minimizing landfill use.
dependencies: Develop clear guidelines for waste management in construction, focusing on waste reduction and material reuse.\nPromote the use of sustainable building materials and circular economy principles in construction projects.\nProvide training and incentives for construction companies to adopt efficient waste management practices.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of contractors complying with the management plan.\nMonthly amount of construction waste recycled or reused (tonnes/month).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions due to proper construction waste management.

action_name: Strengthen Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Systems
description: Enhance processes for returning products to the production cycle, encouraging collection, reuse, and recycling.
dependencies: Develop systems and policies to facilitate product return and integration into the production cycle.\nPromote collection, reuse, and recycling through public awareness campaigns and incentives.\nCollaborate with manufacturers, retailers, and consumers to ensure efficient return and recycling processes.
key_performance_indicators: Quantity of products returned and processed through reverse logistics (units or tons/month).\nPercentage of industrial sectors with active reverse logistics programs.\nAnnual estimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions through material reuse and recycling.

action_name: Improve public transport systems to promote modal shift
description: Implements measures to enhance the coverage, frequency, capacity, speed, reliability, accessibility, resilience, safety, affordability, comfort, and convenience of public transport systems (e.g., buses, BRT, informal transport, intra-city rail). Specific actions include expanding routes, improving service frequency and reliability, integrating ticketing systems, and ensuring universal accessibility. These improvements encourage passengers to shift from private motorized transport to public transport, reducing emissions and supporting more sustainable mobility.
dependencies: Improve the quality of public transportation services to attract passengers from private motorized transport.\nImplement policies and infrastructure that support and enhance the efficiency of public transportation systems.\nPromote awareness of the environmental benefits of public transport to encourage a modal shift and reduce emissions.
key_performance_indicators: Annual increase in the number of passengers using the municipal bus system.\nPercentage of bus routes with improved travel time reliability.\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions due to increased public transportation use.

action_name: Implement energy efficiency criteria and indicators in the procurement of goods, services, or works by the municipal public administration.
description: The architectural projects for all renovations and constructions contracted must be designed to minimize the use of artificial lighting and internal cooling, allowing for the use of natural light and cross ventilation. It sould include all energy end-uses in municipal buildings, promote the use of sustainable materials, and adoption of passive design principles.
dependencies: Architectural designs to prioritize natural light and cross ventilation.\nMinimization of artificial lighting and internal cooling needs in all renovations and constructions.\nCompliance with sustainable building standards in contracted projects.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of municipal procurement contracts including energy efficiency criteria.\nReduction in energy consumption of procured goods or services (kWh/year).\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from energy-efficient public procurement.

action_name: Incentive to create bike-sharing programs in urban areas, with a focus on electric bikes.
description: This action encourages the establishment of bike-sharing systems in cities, specifically promoting the use of electric bicycles. These systems allow residents to rent electric bikes for short trips, reducing the dependence on cars for urban transportation. By integrating electric bikes, cities can further reduce greenhouse gas emissions, alleviate traffic congestion, and promote a healthier and more sustainable mode of transportation for both urban and rural areas. This initiative also supports mobility equality, as it makes bikes more accessible to a wider range of people.
dependencies: Establishment of bike-sharing systems with a focus on electric bicycles to reduce car dependence.\nIntegration of electric bikes to lower greenhouse gas emissions, alleviate traffic congestion, and promote sustainable transportation.\nPromotion of mobility equality by making electric bikes accessible to a wider population.
key_performance_indicators: Number of electric bikes available in bike-sharing programs.\nAnnual increase in bike-sharing users.\nEstimated reduction in CO₂ equivalent emissions from the adoption of electric bike-sharing.

action_name: Establish eco-parks.
description: An eco-park is a facility for the mechanical and biological treatment of urban solid waste, integrating different technologies for the segregation and treatment of various fractions within the waste. This treatment aims to maximize the recovery of dry and organic waste and reduce the volume of waste to be sent for final disposal in landfills, using technologies such as energy generation, composting, recycling recovery, proper disposal of residual waste, and other existing treatment methods available in the market. By integrating these processes , eco-parks operate as multi-technology hubs for waste management, fostering synergies between waste reduction, energy recovery, and environmental protection for the cities. They also contribute to green job creation, climate change mitigation, and urban sustainability.
dependencies: Implementation of eco-parks for mechanical and biological treatment of urban solid waste.\nIntegration of technologies such as energy generation, composting, recycling recovery, and proper disposal of residual waste.\nMaximization of dry and organic waste recovery to reduce landfill disposal volumes.
key_performance_indicators: Total area covered by eco-parks in the city (hectares).\nIncrease in the number of visitors to eco-parks annually.\nImprovement in local biodiversity indices within eco-park areas.

action_name: Improve Accelerate Environmental Regularization of Rural Properties
description: Implement programs to register properties in the Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) and adhere to environmental restoration commitments.
dependencies: Access to digital platforms and technical training for property registration and restoration processes.\nFinancial incentives and partnerships with environmental agencies to support implementation.\nMonitoring and enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance with restoration commitments.
key_performance_indicators: Number of rural properties with regularised Rural Environmental Registration (CAR).\nTotal area of native vegetation protected or restored on regularised properties (hectares).\nAnnual reduction in greenhouse gas emissions (tCO₂e) due to regularisation.

action_name: Establish Municipal Programs for Payment for Environmental Services and other ecological financial incentives
description: Financial incentives such as loans, taxes, grants and rebates can be effective ways to promote ecological conservation and more sustainable practices. Municipalities can initiate schemes or help implement regional or national programmes. Payment for Environmental Services involves paying landowners for maintaining or improving environmental conditions on their properties.
dependencies: Creation of funding mechanisms and clear eligibility criteria with performance indicators.\nPartnerships with environmental organizations and awareness campaigns to encourage participation.\nIntegration with legal frameworks to ensure program sustainability.
key_performance_indicators: Number of active Payment for Environmental Services (PES) contracts signed.\nTotal area under incentivised conservation or restoration practices (hectares).\nAmount of carbon sequestered or emissions avoided through PES actions (tCO₂e/year).

action_name: Prioritize Procurement of Locally Produced Agroecological Products in Public Purchases
description: Focus on buying sustainable, locally produced food for public institutions. Additional actions could include identifying reliable local suppliers, partnering with producers and allocating funding to wider sustainable procurement programs and establishing monitoring systems to ensure compliance with sustainability goals
dependencies: Development of procurement policies and identification of reliable local suppliers.\nPartnerships with producers and allocation of funding for sustainable procurement programs.\nEstablishment of monitoring systems to ensure compliance with sustainability criteria.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of the total volume of public purchases coming from local agroecological producers.\nAmount of CO₂ emissions avoided due to reduced transport distance (tCO₂e).\nNumber of agroecological producers benefiting from public purchases.

action_name: Encourage Local Agroecological Production and Short Supply Chains
description: Support local, sustainable agricultural practices and reduce emissions associated with food transport. Actions could include incentives for local food distribution networks, partnerships with producers and investment in infrastructure to support local markets and policies to prioritize low-emission transportation methods. These should be underpinned by other programmes to encourage local sustainable agriculture methods.
dependencies: Incentives for sustainable agricultural practices and development of local food distribution networks.\nPartnerships with producers and investment in infrastructure to support local markets.\nPolicies to prioritize low-emission transportation methods.
key_performance_indicators: Number of producers adhering to local agroecological practices.\nPercentage of food consumed in the city from short chains.\nReduction in emissions associated with food transport (tCO₂e).

action_name: Replace Inefficient Lighting with LED Technology in Public Spaces
description: This action focuses on replacing outdated and inefficient lighting systems in public spaces with energy-efficient LED technology. The objective is to enhance energy efficiency, reduce operational costs, and lower carbon emissions, contributing to a more sustainable and environmentally-friendly municipal infrastructure.
dependencies: Invest in technology, develop an action plan, and secure funding for LED installation.\nTrain municipal staff on installation and maintenance of energy-efficient lighting.\nEnsure proper maintenance infrastructure to maximize energy savings and reduce emissions.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of public lighting replaced with LED technology (%).\nReduction in public lighting electricity consumption (kWh/year).\nReduction of CO₂ emissions related to public lighting (tCO₂e/year).

action_name: Implement congestion pricing and restrictions on high-polluting vehicles
description: The city introduces congestion pricing and related restrictions (such as tolls, charges, or bans) on high-polluting vehicles that cover significant parts of the city. To ensure equity and social acceptance, design measures may include exemptions or discounts for low-income drivers, reinvestment of revenues into public transport and active mobility, and strong communication campaigns. While congestion pricing can deliver major emission reductions, it requires substantial governance capacity and is best suited for larger metropolitan areas.
dependencies: "Establish a clear legal framework and invest in technology for monitoring and enforcement (e.g., cameras, sensors).","Launch awareness campaigns and ensure availability of efficient public transportation or alternative mobility solutions.","Collaborate with local governments and transport agencies, and set up systems for monitoring and evaluating the policy's effectiveness."
key_performance_indicators: Reduction of CO₂ emissions from urban road transport (tCO₂e/year).\nRevenue generated by the implementation of the urban congestion charge (R$).

action_name: Establish a financial support program for extreme weather events
description: Creation of a program to mitigate the effects of climate tragedies, including financial assistance to affected families, efforts to increase access to affordable hazard insurance, and efforts to secure additional resources for recovery and reconstruction, including partnerships with state and federal government bodies. Recovery and reconstruction measures should include adaptive measures with the emphasis on build back better to withstand future hazards and helping residents retrofit buildings.
dependencies: Financial resources\nEmergency response plans\nInstitutional coordination
key_performance_indicators: Number of people assisted\nCost-effectiveness\nCommunity resilience

action_name: Strengthen the healthcare system to respond effectively to extreme events
description: Improve the infrastructure of healthcare units to assist people who require medical care due to impacts associated with climate risks (climate victims), such as those affected by heat waves or floods, especially in more vulnerable areas. Develop action plans to prepare the healthcare network for extreme climate-related situations.
dependencies: Investment in the renovation and expansion of healthcare facilities, ensuring they are equipped to handle climate-related health impacts, particularly in vulnerable areas.\nDevelopment of action plans and training programs for healthcare professionals to respond to extreme climate events like heatwaves and floods.\nCollaboration with local authorities, emergency response teams, and climate experts to create a comprehensive framework for preparing the healthcare network for climate risks.
key_performance_indicators:
Number of healthcare facilities upgraded for climate-related emergencies.
Increase in healthcare staff trained in climate emergency response (%).
Number of climate-related injuries treated successfully.
.

action_name: Clean and unclog drainage channels and install eco-barriers
description: Cleaning and unclogging channels in the city to reduce the risk of flooding caused by extreme rainfall events. Installation of eco-barriers to assist in cleaning efforts and raise awareness about solid waste.
dependencies: Regular maintenance\nProper waste management practices
key_performance_indicators: Flood reduction\nWaste reduction\nMaintenance costs

action_name: Improve Implementation of urban gardens
description: Identify and assess the feasibility of suitable areas for the installation of urban gardens and ensure that the sites chosen meet the expectations of the community.
dependencies: Ensure availability of detailed land-use maps and urban planning data.\nEngage with local communities to understand their needs and expectations.\nEvaluate soil quality, water availability, and form partnerships to support the establishment and maintenance of gardens.
key_performance_indicators: Number of urban gardens created.\nAmount of locally produced food (kg/year).\nNumber of direct beneficiaries.

action_name: Establish mechanisms for intersectoral coordination and public participation in climate policy
description: Establish more mechanisms that enable better intersectoral coordination and public participation in climate policy, including the creation of working groups with neighboring municipalities to discuss a common climate agenda.
key_performance_indicators: Number of intersectoral meetings held per year.\nPercentage of population participating in climate forums (%).\nNumber of proposals accepted and implemented through public consultations.

action_name: Strengthen programs for control and conservation of protected areas
description: This action focuses on implementing a series of integrated strategies to enhance environmental conservation and maximize its benefits, such as expanding protected areas, developing management plans for conservation units, and training ecotourism guides to strengthen sustainable tourism.
dependencies: Expansion of protected areas to enhance environmental conservation.\nDevelopment of management plans for conservation units.\nTraining of ecotourism guides to promote sustainable tourism.
key_performance_indicators: Percentage increase in area of protected regions (%).\nReduction in deforestation rates in protected areas annually (%).\nNumber of conservation programs strengthened annually.

action_name: Establish a first‑response firefighting brigade
description: Creation of a First Response Brigade in rural communities to provide them with training and equipment for fire prevention and firefighting.
dependencies: Fire prevention education\nOngoing support and resources\nCommunication systems
key_performance_indicators: Response time\nBurned area\nFire suppression effetiveness

action_name: Improve Hydrological Monitoring System with Telemetry Stations
description: Implementation of a hydrological monitoring system with telemetry stations to monitor rainfall, water levels, and meteorological variables in real-time.
dependencies: Equipment and infrastructure\nRobust data management system\nInstitutional coordination
key_performance_indicators: Timeliness of data\nCost-effectiveness\nMitigation effectiveness

action_name: Develop an Environmental Education Plan
description: Design and implement a comprehensive environmental education plan that fosters climate literacy and awareness across schools, communities, and the media. Municipal governments can organize workshops, awareness campaigns, and nature-based activities such as tree planting to reconnect residents with their environment. The plan should integrate themes of climate change, adaptation, mitigation, and climate justice, with particular attention to youth, women, and vulnerable groups. By embedding equity and inclusion, cities can strengthen long-term engagement and empower communities to take part in climate action.
dependencies: Curriculum development\nTeacher training\nCommunity engagement
key_performance_indicators: Reach and participation\nCommunity engagement\nPolicy and program influence

action_name: Establish a Plan for Preparation and Emergency Response Measures in the event of extreme weather events
description: This action focuses on preparing the municipality to respond to extreme events, aiming to provide a rapid response that minimizes the impacts on the population.
dependencies: Development of a comprehensive emergency response plan that includes coordination between local authorities, emergency services, and community organizations\nInvestment in early warning systems and infrastructure to ensure timely and effective responses to extreme events\nTraining and capacity-building for local responders and communities to enhance preparedness and resilience to extreme events
key_performance_indicators: Number of emergency response partnerships established.\nAverage response time during extreme weather events (hours).\nPercentage reduction in casualties and damages during extreme weather events annually (%).

action_name: Build safe housing and implement urban rehabilitation projects for populations living in high-risk areas
description: The priority of this action is to build safe housing and implement urban rehabilitation projects for the population living in areas prone to landslides and flooding, as the housing deficit is one of the main factors related to these threats. This will be implemented through the construction of new housing units in safe locations for family resettlement, and infrastructure upgrades like slope stabilization and improved drainage systems within vulnerable communities.
dependencies: Availability of funding and financial mechanisms to support the construction of safe housing in high-risk areas\nCollaboration with urban planners and engineers to design housing solutions that are resilient to landslides and flooding\nImplementation of policies to regulate land use and prevent informal settlements in areas vulnerable to climate risks
key_performance_indicators: Number of safe housing units constructed annually.\nPercentage reduction in population living in high-risk areas (%).\nNumber of urban rehabilitation projects completed annually.

action_name: Improve the hydrometeorological forecasting, monitoring, and alert system for climate risks
description: This action aims to expand the procedures related to the existing climate risk forecasting, monitoring, and alert system in the municipality.
key_performance_indicators: Number of weather stations installed and operational.\nAverage time between alerts and weather events (hours).\nPercentage reduction in damage caused by extreme weather events annually (%).

action_name: Develop and implement the Municipal Risk Reduction Plan (PMRR) and identify population groups vulnerable to climate risks.
description: This action aims to strengthen the development of the Municipal Risk Reduction Plan (PMRR) in the municipality, as it is a highly relevant tool for managing climate risks, especially river floods and landslides.
dependencies: Availability of technical expertise and resources to develop and implement the Municipal Risk Reduction Plan (PMRR)\nData collection and analysis to accurately assess climate risks, especially related to river floods and landslides\nPolitical commitment and coordination between various government agencies to integrate the PMRR into broader urban planning and disaster management strategies
key_performance_indicators: Percentage of vulnerable population covered by MRRP (%).\nNumber of risk reduction measures implemented annually.\nReduction in the number of people affected by climate-related disasters annually.

action_name: Preventive maintenance of drainage systems
description: Regular upkeep and cleaning of urban drainage systems, including storm drains, sewers, and retention basins, to ensure efficient water flow and prevent blockages that can lead to flooding during heavy rainfall events.
dependencies: Budget allocation for maintenance activities\nRegular inspections to identify potential issues
key_performance_indicators: Number of drainage blockages cleared.\nPercentage of drainage systems in good condition.\nNumber of reported flood incidents.

action_name: Develop a Climate Action Plan
description: A comprehensive plan outlining a city's strategies and actions to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and adapt to the impacts of climate change which typically includes an assessment of the city's climate risks and vulnerabilities, setting emission reduction targets, and implementation of actions across various sectors such as energy, transportation, waste management, and urban planning.
dependencies: Political will and commitment from government\nStakeholder engagement and collaboration\nFunding and resources for implementation
key_performance_indicators: Greenhouse gas emission reduction targets.\nNumber of climate adaptation actions implemented.\nInvestment in climate mitigation and adaptation projects.

action_name: Redirect urban development through climate‑risk spatial planning
description: Mapping of critical flood-prone areas with the aim of revising and harmonizing legislation related to land use, given the intensification of the impacts of extreme weather events.
dependencies: Mapping of critical flood-prone areas to address risks from extreme weather events.\nRevision and harmonization of land-use legislation to mitigate flood impacts.\nIntegration of climate resilience considerations into urban planning policies.
key_performance_indicators: Number of zoning and land-use plans updated based on mapping data.\nTime reduction in emergency response to mapped flood-prone areas (hours).\nPercentage of flood-prone areas with early-warning systems installed

action_name: Expand urban green-blue networks and corridors
description: Expand and connect urban green spaces and blue-green infrastructure (BGI) in the public realm. Actions include street tree planting, establishing green corridors/greenways, pocket and large parks, and green-blue features (bioswales, rain gardens, permeable surfaces) to manage stormwater, reduce urban heat, enhance biodiversity, and support carbon sequestration. Embedding these measures in urban planning strengthens ecosystem services, resilience, and livability.
dependencies: Expansion of permeable and semi-permeable areas in City-administered buildings and public spaces.\nAdoption of nature-based solutions (NbS) such as urban tree planting, green roofs, rainwater cisterns, and bio-swales.\nFeasibility analyses for permeable pavements and increased green areas in roadways, alongside traditional stormwater management solutions like curbs, gutters, and retention ponds.
key_performance_indicators: Reduction in surface water runoff during rainfall events (%).\nDecrease in flooding occurrences in modified areas.\nPercentage of public spaces complying with new permeable surface regulations.

action_name: Restore in Vulnerable Areas
description: A comprehensive project addressing the socio-environmental vulnerability of an informal settlement. It includes relocating residents from flood-prone areas, restoring the environment, and providing infrastructure and social services.
dependencies: Adequate funding\nInter-agency coordination\nLand tenure security
key_performance_indicators: Number of households relocated.\nEnvironmental restoration progress.\nFlood risk reduction.

action_name: Develop an Urban Afforestation Plan
description: This action focuses on expanding green areas in the city through urban afforestation. This includes planting trees in sidewalks, squares, public buildings, and schools, as well as creating ecological parks to revitalize watercourses and/or restore forests.
dependencies: Water resources\nLong-term maintenance
key_performance_indicators: Area of green spaces created or restored\nCommunity use of green spaces\nWater usage and conservation

action_name: Implement Multi-hazard Early Warning Systems (MH-EWS)
description: Early Warning systems involve the timely detection and communication of potential climate-related hazards, enabling proactive responses to mitigate risks and enhancing community preparedness. This includes intense rains and landslides, using a network of telemetry stations to monitor rainfall and other weather conditions, with clear trigger thresholds to issue public alerts (sirens/alarms, SMS/cell broadcast, radio/PA) in case of potential flooding or landslides.
dependencies: Reliable monitoring network\nCommunity education and preparedness\nInstitutional coordination
key_performance_indicators: Timeliness and accuracy of warnings\nNumber of lives saved and injuries prevented\nReduction in economic losses

action_name: Upgrade Slope stabilization and drainage
description: This action involves stabilizing slopes and maintaining or restoring drainage systems in hillside areas. This helps to prevent landslides and erosion, reducing the risk of disasters.
dependencies: Geotechnical and hydrological studies\nLand-use planning and regulation\nMonitoring and maintenance
key_performance_indicators: Number of slopes stabilized\nReduction in landslide occurrences\nPerformance of drainage systems

action_name: Improve Creation of An Epidemiological Intelligence Center
description: This action focuses on establishing an epidemiological intelligence center to monitor public health indicators and provide accessible information to the population. This helps in making informed decisions and protecting public health, particularly in relation to climate-sensitive diseases.
dependencies: Implementation of Epidemiological Intelligence Center\nData collection and infrastructure\nInter-agency collaboration
key_performance_indicators: Disease surveillance\nHealth system preparedness\nCommunity health outcomes

action_name: Implement integrated coastal zone management
description: This action describes the implementation of an integrated coastal zone management plan to promote sustainable development and address the impacts of climate change in coastal areas. It includes measures to mitigate the impacts of sea-level rise and coastal erosion.
dependencies: "Comprehensive planning and design","Construction and engineering expertise","Land-use planning","Development of a geospatial data system to assess and monitor the environmental vulnerability of different coastal sections and inform management decisions.","Collaboration with environmental experts, local authorities and beach permit holders to implement sustainable practices and regulations in coastal areas."
key_performance_indicators: Flood frequency and severity\nDrainage system capacity\nInfrastructure condition

action_name: Create an Environmental Health Surveillance Program related to Populations Exposed to Air Pollution, Noise Pollution, Water Pollution, and Soil Pollution.
description: Develop actions aimed at promoting the health of the population exposed to environmental factors related to atmospheric, noise, and sanitation pollutants. Identify and evaluate the acute and chronic risks and effects of exposure to fixed and mobile sources of air, noise, water, and soil pollution, and act in the surveillance of diseases derived from these pollutants through physical units and work groups, especially among the most vulnerable people.
dependencies: Investment in environmental monitoring systems to assess air, noise, and water pollution levels across the city.\nTraining of health and environmental surveillance teams to evaluate and address risks associated with pollutant exposure.\nCreation of policies and regulations that reduce pollution from industries and vehicles, and promote clean technologies in vulnerable areas.
key_performance_indicators: Reduction in exposure levels of pollutants among vulnerable populations (%).\nFrequency of health alerts issued and acted upon.\nNumber of individuals receiving medical assistance due to environmental health issues.
